title: Narasimha Avatar: The Lion Who Stepped Out of a Pillar
sources: Bhagavata Purana, Canto 7, chapters 2-10 (Hiranyakashipu's penance and Brahma's boon, Prahlada's devotion, the attempts on his life, the pillar, Narasimha at twilight on the threshold, Prahlada's prayers)
Vishnu Purana, Book 1, chapters 17-20 (Prahlada and Hiranyakashipu)

lines.text: Long ago, a demon king named Hiranyakashipu prayed for years, until Brahma offered him a wish.
lines.caps: LONG *AGO | A *DEMON KING | NAMED *HIRANYAKASHIPU | PRAYED | FOR *YEARS | UNTIL *BRAHMA | OFFERED HIM | A *WISH
lines.say: Long ago, a demon king named Hirun-yuh-kushipoo prayed for years, until Bruhma offered him a wish.

lines.text: He asked that no man or beast could harm him,
lines.caps: HE *ASKED | THAT NO *MAN | OR *BEAST | COULD *HARM HIM

lines.text: by day or by night, indoors or outdoors,
lines.caps: BY *DAY | OR BY *NIGHT | *INDOORS | OR *OUTDOORS

lines.text: on the earth or in the sky, by any weapon.
lines.caps: ON THE *EARTH | OR IN THE *SKY | BY ANY *WEAPON

lines.text: Feeling invincible, he ordered the whole world to worship him alone.
lines.caps: FEELING *INVINCIBLE | HE *ORDERED | THE WHOLE *WORLD | TO *WORSHIP | HIM *ALONE

lines.text: But his own little son, Prahlada, loved Vishnu with all his heart.
lines.caps: BUT HIS OWN | LITTLE *SON | *PRAHLADA | LOVED *VISHNU | WITH ALL HIS *HEART
lines.say: But his own little son, Pruh-lahda, loved Vishnu with all his heart.

lines.text: The furious king tried everything to break him, wild elephants, serpents, even fire.
lines.caps: THE *FURIOUS KING | TRIED *EVERYTHING | TO *BREAK HIM | WILD *ELEPHANTS | *SERPENTS | EVEN *FIRE

lines.text: Each time, the boy simply prayed, and walked away unharmed.
lines.caps: EACH *TIME | THE BOY | SIMPLY *PRAYED | AND WALKED AWAY | *UNHARMED

lines.text: At last the king roared, where is your Vishnu? Is he in this pillar?
lines.caps: AT *LAST | THE KING *ROARED | *WHERE | IS YOUR *VISHNU? | IS HE | IN THIS *PILLAR?

lines.text: He is everywhere, said Prahlada.
lines.caps: HE IS *EVERYWHERE | SAID *PRAHLADA

lines.text: The king struck the pillar, and it cracked with a sound like thunder.
lines.caps: THE KING *STRUCK | THE *PILLAR | AND IT *CRACKED | WITH A SOUND | LIKE *THUNDER

lines.text: Out stepped Narasimha, half man, half lion, neither man nor beast.
lines.caps: OUT *STEPPED | *NARASIMHA | HALF *MAN | HALF *LION | NEITHER MAN | NOR *BEAST
lines.say: Out stepped Nara-sim-ha, half man, half lion, neither man nor beast.

lines.text: It was twilight, neither day nor night.
lines.caps: IT WAS *TWILIGHT | NEITHER *DAY | NOR *NIGHT

lines.text: He stood on the doorstep, neither indoors nor outdoors,
lines.caps: HE STOOD | ON THE *DOORSTEP | NEITHER *INDOORS | NOR *OUTDOORS

lines.text: lifted the king onto his lap, neither earth nor sky,
lines.caps: *LIFTED | THE KING | ONTO HIS *LAP | NEITHER *EARTH | NOR *SKY

lines.text: and with his claws alone, he ended the tyrant's reign.
lines.caps: AND WITH HIS *CLAWS | *ALONE | HE *ENDED | THE TYRANT'S *REIGN

lines.text: Every word of the wish was kept, and still it could not save him.
lines.caps: EVERY *WORD | OF THE *WISH | WAS *KEPT | AND *STILL | IT COULD NOT | *SAVE HIM

lines.text: Only little Prahlada was unafraid. He walked up, and the lion's fury melted into a smile.
lines.caps: ONLY LITTLE | *PRAHLADA | WAS *UNAFRAID | HE *WALKED UP | AND THE LION'S *FURY | *MELTED | INTO A *SMILE
lines.say: Only little Pruh-lahda was unafraid. He walked up, and the lion's fury melted into a smile.

lines.text: Narasimha blessed the boy, and made him king.
lines.caps: NARASIMHA | *BLESSED | THE *BOY | AND MADE HIM *KING
lines.say: Nara-sim-ha blessed the boy, and made him king.

lines.text: This is Narasimha, the fourth avatar of Vishnu,
lines.caps: THIS IS *NARASIMHA | THE *FOURTH | *AVATAR | OF *VISHNU
lines.say: This is Nara-sim-ha, the fourth avatar of Vishnu,

lines.text: a reminder that no power can shield cruelty, and that faith fears nothing.
lines.caps: A *REMINDER | NO *POWER | CAN *SHIELD | *CRUELTY | AND THAT *FAITH | FEARS *NOTHING
